[27:46] Yeah, that's a really important question.
[27:49] And, you know, by the way, like security and AI,
[27:53] that came up a lot with the meetings we had at the CFTC,
[27:57] the advisory committee kind of across the whole industry.
[27:59] And so I think, you know, our approach,
[28:01] we're very, I think, well positioned with our approach here.
[28:06] You know, we approach security in layers
[28:07] and because we're in Ethereum L2,
[28:10] we have that structure by design.
[28:12] So every state change on lighter executed
[28:15] is executed by the sequencer
[28:17] and then proven by the ZK circuits
[28:19] and verified by our contracts on Ethereum
[28:21] with Guardians in between.
[28:23] So what that means is that the sequencer and the circuits
[28:25] enforce the same rules for separate implementations.
[28:28] So each acts as a cross-check on the other.
[28:32] We think about this as the Swiss cheese model.
[28:34] So there's a lot of redundancy built in to our architecture.
[28:39] On top of that, we run security reviews
[28:41] and testing with our internal team, outside teams.
[28:44] And we have a lot of, you know, our team actually,
[28:48] as some of you know, we were AI builders before
[28:50] who started working on lighter.
[28:51] So we have a deep understanding of all the different AI tools
[28:58] as well as connectivity within that space.
[29:00] So we're, you know, very actively using AI tools,
[29:03] including from kind of basic testing
[29:06] to formal verification.
[29:07] And we're working on formally verifying
[29:11] our most critical components through that.
[29:14] And finally, you know,
[29:15] our architecture gives us a natural window
[29:18] because there is a lag between the execution
[29:20] and finalization of Ethereum.
[29:21] If something does go wrong,
[29:23] there's time to monitor that activity
[29:25] and respond before, you know,
